gaps.sentence: Every one of the switches ___ been tested twice.
gaps.explanation: 'Every one of' takes a singular verb: has.

gaps.sentence: There's ___ point in complaining — no one will listen.
gaps.hint: fixed expression: ___ point in doing something
gaps.explanation: 'There's little point in doing something' means it is hardly worth doing; 'point' is uncountable here.
'Far too much information' is the correct intensifier pattern; 'far much' and 'far very' do not exist.

gaps.sentence: There are too ___ tourists in Venice in August.
gaps.explanation: 'Too many' is used before countable plurals like tourists; 'too much' is for uncountables.

gaps.hint: general statement without 'the' — 'people' has no article
gaps.explanation: 'Most people' means people in general; 'most of' needs 'the' (most of the people).

gaps.sentence: We had ___ luggage that the taxi couldn't take it all.
gaps.explanation: 'So much luggage that …' — luggage is uncountable.

gaps.sentence: The hall was so crowded that ___ found a seat.
gaps.hint: a crowded hall means no one succeeded
gaps.explanation: 'So crowded that nobody found a seat' matches the logic of the sentence; 'anybody' cannot be the subject of an affirmative clause.

gaps.hint: an unspecified day in the future
gaps.explanation: 'Another day' means some other, unspecified day; 'the other day' refers to the recent past.
